title: Star Wars: A New Hope
synopsis: Tatooine. Two suns. Aunt Beru's blue milk. A droid you bought yesterday is, apparently, carrying the plans to a planet-killing weapon. Buckle up.

nodes.text: You stand watching them set. You want to be anywhere else. Both choices lead to The Droids, but “Stay loyal to the farm” arrives there with a different cost than “Plan to leave.” By The Droids, the system will have recorded that choice as precedent.

choices.consequence: You choose to stay loyal to the farm. By The Droids, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to plan to leave. By The Droids, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: R2 has a message for an Obi-Wan Kenobi. Uncle Owen says forget it. The road still runs toward Sandcrawler Wreck. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Chase R2 at dawn” and choosing “Tell Uncle.”

choices.consequence: You choose to chase R2 at dawn. By Sandcrawler Wreck, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to tell Uncle. By Sandcrawler Wreck, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Stormtroopers killed the Jawas. The droids, you realize, are wanted. You cannot avoid Aunt and Uncle; you can only decide whether “Run home” or “Hide the droids” defines the person who reaches it. In Sandcrawler Wreck, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You choose to run home. By Aunt and Uncle, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You commit to hide the droids. It carries you toward Aunt and Uncle, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: They are dead, the homestead burning. You stand in the smoke. Ben will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Vow” than after “Mourn.” At Ben, the decision will matter as data as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You vow. The path to Ben opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You mourn. The path to Ben opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Obi-Wan tells you the truth about your father. He hands you a lightsaber. Cantina will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Take it” than after “Pause.” By Cantina, the system will have recorded that choice as precedent.

choices.consequence: You commit to take it. It carries you toward Cantina, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You commit to pause. It carries you toward Cantina, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Mos Eisley. Aliens. A pilot with a Wookiee. The Falcon is already waiting. What changes is whether “Hire Han” or “Look for another captain” is the instinct you carry into it. At The Falcon, the decision will matter as data as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You hire Han. The path to The Falcon opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You look for another captain. The path to The Falcon opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Lasers. Towers. Wedge falls back. Biggs goes down. Vader Behind comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Stay on target” and “Veer to avoid.” In Trench Run, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You choose to whoop. By Medals, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Leia gives you and Han medals. Chewie is, briefly, snubbed. The road still runs toward After. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Notice the Chewie thing publicly” and choosing “Be polite.” By After, the system will have recorded that choice as precedent.

nodes.text: The Rebellion has many fights ahead. The galaxy is still mostly the Empire. The road still runs toward Your Father's Saber. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Stay with the Rebellion” and choosing “Take a season off.”

choices.consequence: You stay with the Rebellion. The path to Your Father's Saber opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You take a season off. The path to Your Father's Saber opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You hold it in your hand. The weight is real. The path, you realize, is yours. “Train” draws you toward Becoming a Jedi; “Train slowly” leaves The Best Pilot waiting on the other side. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Bringing Balance in play.

choices.consequence: You choose to train. By Becoming a Jedi, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to train slowly. By The Best Pilot, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You choose to take the third path. By Bringing Balance, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: You find Yoda. You train. You meet your father. You become, in time, the Jedi the galaxy needed. The Force, you decide, is family. The road into Becoming a Jedi began with “Train” in Your Father's Saber; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You stay with Rogue Squadron. You fly forever. Han calls you kid for the rest of your life. You never quite mind it. The road into The Best Pilot began with “Train slowly” in Your Father's Saber; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

Years later you start a new Jedi Order. The first new students are not all young. The Force, you teach them, is older than any of them. The road into Bringing Balance began with “Take the third path” in Your Father's Saber; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
